title: Agreeing & Disagreeing
description: Respond to an opinion with respectful agreement or disagreement.
objectives: Respond to an opinion with respectful agreement or disagreement.

stages.title: Understand the language
stages.instructions: Read the explanation, examples, common error, and recap.

blocks.text: This lesson prepares you to respond to an opinion with respectful agreement or disagreement. The central language is agreement phrases and polite contrast. It belongs to the practical context of opinions, technology & social life. Focus first on meaning: decide what information the listener needs. Then choose the subject, verb form, and useful detail. At A2, connect the main message to a time, reason, contrast, or result. Listen for context before choosing the tense or functional phrase. The same language returns in the listening, repeat, speaking, exercises, and guided conversation stages.

blocks.english: I agree with you about online safety.
blocks.explanation: Use this model to begin the agreeing & disagreeing exchange.

blocks.english: I see your point, but I prefer meeting in person.
blocks.explanation: This agreeing & disagreeing model adds a different detail or response.
Use this question or response to keep the agreeing & disagreeing exchange moving.

blocks.text: Notice the two models: “I agree with you about online safety.” and “I see your point, but I prefer meeting in person.” They show the pattern in complete communication, not as isolated grammar. Say the model aloud, replace one detail, and check that the new sentence keeps the intended meaning. When the other person asks a follow-up question, answer directly and add a relevant detail. This makes the exchange natural while keeping the language controlled. Compare the time and viewpoint in each model, and use a linker when two ideas need a clear relationship. Avoid adding advanced forms when the lesson pattern already communicates the message accurately.

blocks.title: Common error
blocks.text: Do not mix the word order or verb form with another pattern. Keep the controlled form for this lesson: agreement phrases and polite contrast.

items: Communicative goal: Respond to an opinion with respectful agreement or disagreement.

Use one clear model, add a relevant detail, and respond to the other speaker.
